messages:
Maya: Quick sync — running a 30m rapid-fire "battle lab" tomorrow to finalize competitive hooks for the launch. Focus: benchmark narrative, one-liner rebuttals, inbound routing rules for leads, and webinar intros. Who can make it? :mega:
Ethan: I can do 30m starting 10:00 PT. Need clear battlecard asks — SDR vs AE routing thresholds and 3 prioritized claims.
Jo: +1. Will bring the latest latency and cost-per-token numbers vs CloudX and LLMAPI.
Samira: I’ll bring webinar hooks and the live demo flow. Also want to test the “unified runtime” messaging against infra vendors.
Devon: I’ll prep quick customer proof points — Dedicated + Private wins (SLA + isolation). Also have a tiny case study about fallback policies.
Maya: Perfect. Agenda: 1) pick 3 headline claims (latency/cost/reliability) 2) craft 6 short rebut bullets 3) routing YAML to validate 4) webinar hook script (15s, 30s).
Ethan: For claims I'd propose: "Consistent p95 latency at production scale", "30–50% lower per-token unit cost w/ batching & caching", "Built-in fallbacks for degraded capacity" — simple and measurable. Thoughts?
Jo: Agree. For the numbers I have: p50 60ms, p95 210ms on our Dedicated pool for a 2k seq gen test; CloudX p95 ~420ms. Cost: our unit cost ~0.6x CloudX for identical model size when caching/batching enabled. Can share a slide.
Samira: Those are good. For rebuts we should have 6 ultra-short lines: 
- "Cloud APIs: simple, but noisy pricing at scale."
- "Self-host: flexible, but ops heavy and unpredictable."
- "Redwood: predictable unit economics + dev UX."
Keep <140 chars each.
Maya: Love the short rebut style. Ethan — can you draft the 6 lines after the meeting?
Ethan: Yeah will do. Also: let's add one tight stat about fallbacks: "automatic routing to smaller models reduces 5xxs by 92% during spikes" — Devon, do you have that stat?
Devon: Yep pulled from canary logs last month. I'll paste the query and raw numbers in the doc.
launch-bot: Reminder: marketing-battle-lab event in #marketing scheduled for 2024-04-03 10:00 PT.
Maya: Routing rules — quick proposal we can test in the lab (SDR vs AE):
```yaml
routing:
  priority:
    - if: "company_employee_count >= 500"
      route: AE
    - if: "annual_spend_estimate >= 200000"
      route: AE
    - else: route: SDR
  tags: [benchmarked, webinar-led, high-touch]
```
Samira: Can we add a path for compliance requests -> Field Eng? E.g., if wants private deployment or KMS, route to Field Eng (AE+Solutions).
Maya: Yes add rule: if interest_tags contains "private" or "kms" -> Field Eng. Also add quick screening question in form: "Data residency required? (yes/no)"
Jo: For webinar hooks, can we test three openers: 
A) "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and cost."
B) "Stop guessing at inference economics — get a real unit cost."
C) "When models and hardware change, your serving layer shouldn't."
Samira: A>B>C in terms of conversion in my past tests. A is product-y, B is quant, C is strategic. We should A/B A vs B in the registration landing.
Ethan: I'll wire up two short landing copies for A/B and route 50/50 traffic from the webinar signup. Samira — need your 15s and 30s script variants by EOD.
Samira: On it. 15s draft: "Redwood Inference gives teams predictable latency and clear per-token economics so you can ship LLM features without surprise bills."
Maya: Nice. Last: deliverables from the lab: final set of 6 rebut bullets, 3 headline claims, routing YAML validated, A/B landing copies, 15/30s scripts, and a one-slide benchmark summary.
Devon: I’ll own the benchmark slide and paste query + raw counts.
Ethan: I’ll own landing copy + compile rebut bullets.
Jo: I’ll own the numbers and a short slide of test methodology.
Samira: I’ll own webinar scripts + the demo runbook.
Maya: Great — 10:00 PT tomorrow, 30m. If anyone needs prep materials uploaded, drop into the thread and tag @Maya. :rocket:
